jobs.description:
Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.

If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.

Role Overview

Lambda is seeking a Technical Program Manager (TPM) to own the integrated delivery program for new data center builds, from the handoff of a selected site by Real Estate through construction, commissioning, operational readiness, and turnover to Network Deployment. You will be the single source of truth for milestones, risks, and dependencies on your sites, leading internal teams and external partners (GCs, design firms, utilities, and vendors) across site work, utilities, shell, MEP, controls, white space, inspections, and commissioning.

Ambiguity is high, timelines are compressed, and the stakes are central to company growth. As we scale beyond our first sites, you will help build the playbooks and governance that let us run many concurrent deployments well.

What You’ll Do

Own the integrated schedule from site handoff to Operations; break builds into workstreams with clear owners and milestones, and actively manage the critical path and schedule compression.

Drive the delivery sequence from rack requirements to engineering criteria, design, plan set, permitting, construction, commissioning, and turnover for MW-scale, high-density (including liquid-cooled) capacity.

Lead cross-functional execution with Real Estate (site assumptions, fiber, permit path), Energy and Utilities (interconnection, substation, power delivery), Engineering (requirements in the design and plan set), Procurement (long-lead equipment), Construction Management (GC schedule, field progress, inspections), Commissioning (test plans, acceptance), Operations (staffing, procedures, access), and Security, and Finance (requirements, budget, CapEx), and Legal.

Manage risk and governance: maintain risk registers, dependency logs, decision trackers, and schedule variance reports; surface permitting, utility, design, procurement, sequencing, and commissioning risks early.

Escalate with facts: status, baseline vs. forecast date, variance, impact, owner, mitigation options, and decision date. Lead schedule recovery when milestones slip.

Hold partners accountable to contractual milestones, production and shipping schedules, and commercial commitments while maintaining productive relationships.

Communicate to leadership through program reviews and concise, high-signal status updates.

Deliver clean turnover: define handover criteria and ensure white space, power, cooling, controls, cable pathways, access, and documentation are ready for Network Deployment.

Scale the function: build repeatable playbooks, dashboards, and lessons-learned loops across concurrent deployments.

Travel (~40%) to sites to validate progress and build partner relationships.

Scope of Ownership

Owns: site-level delivery program management; the integrated schedule; cross-functional coordination; milestone, risk, dependency, and decision tracking; variance reporting and escalation; Operations readiness.

Partners on, but does not own: site selection and real estate; engineering design authority; construction means and methods and GC management; commissioning authority; procurement commercial strategy; network and services deployment; steady-state operations.

You

Have 7+ years in data center delivery, infrastructure or construction program management, mission-critical facilities, or large capital projects.

Have delivered ground-up data centers or comparable mission-critical, industrial, semiconductor, or energy facilities, ideally multi-site on compressed timelines.

Know the full lifecycle: site handoff, permitting, design, utilities, procurement, construction, MEP, controls, commissioning, and turnover.

Run integrated schedules, critical path, dependency logs, and change control with rigor.

Understand technical tradeoffs well enough to spot risks, ask precise questions, and escalate without owning design authority.

Align partners, vendors, and engineering teams around shared deliverables, and bridge physical infrastructure with network and security teams.

Make sound decisions with incomplete information under schedule pressure, and communicate status clearly to executives.

Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Nice to Have

Hyperscale, AI/GPU, cloud region, or high-density compute delivery experience.

Utility interconnection, substation, MV/HV power, and liquid cooling experience.

Work with colocation providers, GCs, EPCs, commissioning agents, and permitting authorities.

PMP, construction management, engineering, or project controls certification.

Success Measures

Sites reach infrastructure turnover on the committed timeline.

Milestones across engineering, construction, commissioning, operations, procurement, and utilities are visible and accurate.

Critical path risks are escalated early with a clear owner, impact, and mitigation options.

Handoff to Operations meets defined readiness criteria, with no major gaps.

Salary Range Information

The annual salary range for this position has been set based on market data and other factors. However, a salary higher or lower than this range may be appropriate for a candidate whose qualifications differ meaningfully from those listed in the job description.

About Lambda

Founded in 2012, with 500+ employees, and growing fast

Our investors notably include TWG Global, US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Andra Capital, SGW, Andrej Karpathy, ARK Invest, Fincadia Advisors, G Squared, In-Q-Tel (IQT), KHK & Partners, NVIDIA, Pegatron, Supermicro, Wistron, Wiwynn, Gradient Ventures, Mercato Partners, SVB, 1517, and Crescent Cove

We have research papers accepted at top machine learning and graphics conferences, including NeurIPS, ICCV, SIGGRAPH, and TOG

Our values are publicly available: https://lambda.ai/careers

We offer generous cash & equity compensation

Health, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents

Wellness and commuter stipends for select roles

401k Plan with 2% company match (USA employees)

Flexible paid time off plan that we all actually use

Equal Opportunity Employer

Lambda is an Equal Opportunity employer. Applicants are considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, national origin, age, sex, gender, marital status, sexual orientation and identity, genetic information, veteran status, citizenship, or any other factors prohibited by local, state, or federal law.

jobs.description:
Overview of the role

We’re on a mission to modernize insurance, making it simpler, more accessible, and customer-first. The insurance industry is a $1T market that has remained largely untouched by the digital revolution, and PolicyMe is here to change that. As a remote-first, Toronto-based startup with big ambitions, we’re looking for a Senior IT Manager to lead the IT Support function as we expand into the next chapter!

What you'll be doing:

You will be a senior member of the team, and a cross-functional leader within PolicyMe. This is an opportunity to completely reshape the IT strategy and execution as PolicyMe moves to the next stage of scale and growth, building durable policies and process that will be used for years to come! You will be the decision-maker! In your day-to-day, this will lead you to:

Define the vision and roadmap for IT Support: You will articulate the strategic goals for the IT Support team and define the roadmap for how we get there. You will communicate progress against the roadmap and goals to all key stakeholders (e.g. Business Operations, Engineering, Leadership, People and Culture).

Hands-on ownership of IT equipment: You will take on the direct responsible of ensuring PolicyMe employees have continuous access to the tools they need (laptops, external monitors, etc.), while also ensuring the inventory management and disposal follow proper governance. This will include managing budgets and strategic thinking on equipment selection decisions.

Prioritize what to work on: You will have to decide what other IT Support team members invest time on and in what order. By developing and executing a disciplined process, you will prioritize process improvements, security rollouts, bugs and maintenance activities.

Collaborate in PolicyMe’s Information Security Committee: You will work closely with senior leaders from Business Operations and Engineering to maintain a robust information security program where your direct responsibilities will include ownership of access control and maintenance of PolicyMe’s SOC 2 certification. This requires deep attention to detail on role-based access control and third party vendor management.

Coordinate on-call availability: You will be responsible for designing and executing alongside the IT support team, on support availability timelines and SLAs within the company based on defined priority levels.

Develop the backlog: You will ideate with stakeholders across PolicyMe and then manage a backlog of new IT initiatives to meet our employee’s needs, improve our back-end integrity, innovate and ultimately reach the defined vision.

Rally the team behind secure best practices: You will serve as the central point across all functions and ensure that any IT-equipment and access-related roadblocks are removed to achieve success. This includes ensuring information security and IT-related governance is well understood and communicated across the organization.

Coordinate the launch: You will work with the Engineering and Business Operations teams to ensure that the patches and new security releases has been thoroughly tested and are ready to launch.

Measure and learn: You will measure the key metrics for our IT support team and report out to the broader organization.

What are we looking for:

Relevant IT support experience: You have 3-5 years of experience in IT support management, Information Security, or Engineering, preferably in a start-up or scale-up technology setting. You can speak to your track record of leading projects and delivering measurable results.

A hands-on aptitude: You have the ability to both think and plan strategically while also remaining a “do-er” for the day to day tasks and activities. This hands-on attitude is incredibly important at PolicyMe and flows through our culture even at the most senior levels.

AI mindset and willingness to innovate: You are excited about the opportunities that AI presents for the IT area and are actively learning about new applications and technologies. You are keen to play a major role in the transition of PolicyMe’s AI adoption and development of AI-first capabilities.

Exceptional collaboration skills: You have high emotional intelligence and can "be the glue" between many different stakeholders in the organization.

Curiosity and highly comfortable with technical topics: You are naturally curious about how everything works. You will work closely with some wicked smart Engineers, so you know when to ask clarifying questions and are not shy about diving into complex topics.

A mindset for risk identification and assessment: You understand that the PolicyMe business model inherently handles high sensitive personal information. You take a risk-mindful approach to problem solving and identify risks before they present themselves as problems. You are comfortable assessing the probability and severity of risks and communicate these clearly.

Strong problem solving skills: You have the ability to take an ambiguous problem and structure it yourself. You are someone who can start with an idea and manage it from concept to deployment. You present and execute solutions that are durable, that is they will solve today’s problem and tomorrow’s edge case!

Strategic decision making: You can balance tradeoffs and consider many side to a problem before arriving at a decision. Decisions are based on strong supporting data, consider the second and third order impacts, and are communicated concisely and clearly.

Why join us:

Generous PTO - 20 vacation days

A comprehensive benefits plan with premiums paid in full by PolicyMe

Investment in your professional development, including an L&D budget, AI tooling budget, performance reviews twice a year and ongoing feedback to ensure you reach your highest potential

An extremely high performing, low-ego, remote-first team that is truly disrupting an old industry

Option to work from home or our Toronto-based office (bonus: we cover the costs to bring all our employees in-person twice a year for experiential socials!)

Access to stock options based on performance

Compensation: The total target cash compensation for this role is $132,000–$154,000 CAD, based on experience. We’ll walk through the details together during the interview.

Compensation

Additional Information

About PolicyMe:

At PolicyMe, we are Canada’s leading digital insurance solution, offering straightforward and affordable financial protection for families from coast to coast. Our product suite includes Life Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, and Health & Dental Insurance, all tailored to Canadians' evolving needs. We also offer B2B2C solutions, partnering with organizations to provide seamless digital insurance options. Founded by a team of insurance experts and technology entrepreneurs, PolicyMe is committed to making insurance simpler and more accessible. Since our launch in 2018, we have grown exponentially, selling over $20 billion in insurance coverage to Canadians.

We are proud of the team we’ve built and are excited for those that are yet to join us. We operate with a remote-first culture, attracting top talent from across Canada. If you’re looking for a fast-paced, collaborative environment, working alongside incredibly ambitious yet humble humans, we may be the right place for you! To learn more, visit www.policyme.com.

Additional Notes:

Job Vacancy: This role reflects growth in our team and expanded operational scope. We’re hiring to support increasing demand and continue delivering an exceptional customer experience.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity: PolicyMe is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and provide fair consideration regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.

Accessibility Statement: We are committed to providing an accessible hiring experience. If you require accommodations during the application process, please indicate this in the “Additional Information” section of your application.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.description:
About the role 

At Apaleo, we're building the open, API-first property management platform for hospitality. With integrations across hundreds of apps through the Apaleo Store, and the first AI agent marketplace for hospitality in our Agent Hub, we simplify operations, elevate the guest journey and drive revenue growth for our customers. 

We're looking for a senior Product Manager to ownin our AI product domain. You'll turn our AI capabilities into coherent, commercially viable products that solve real operational problems for hoteliers. Your goal is to help hotels move towards genuinely autonomous operations, not to ship isolated automations or AI assistants. 

This is not a backlog role. You'll take an ambiguous opportunity, find the right customer problems, define the proposition, build it with Engineering, bring it to market and drive adoption. You'll also play a central role in turning our AI capabilities into a meaningful and growing source of revenue. 

This is a senior individual contributor role with real autonomy. You won't receive a roadmap and execute it. You'll shape it along our vision, using customer insight, data and sound reasoning. You’ll work closely with Engineering, Design, Sales, Marketing and Customer Success, and in close collaboration with our other value stream teams. 

What you'll be up to 

Productising and commercialising our AI capabilities. Define the proposition, target customers and use cases, and shape packaging and launch with commercial teams. 

Building the foundations for AI across our ecosystem. Shape how our AI capabilities understand each hotel's context and work reliably with Apaleo and connected systems across operational areas. 

Productising hospitality knowledge. Turn hospitality expertise and operational processes into scalable product experiences, with appropriate human oversight. 

Driving autonomy and measurable value. Think in complete outcomes, such as staff hours saved and manual work removed. Show hoteliers tangible ROI. 

Driving adoption. Run discovery, shape onboarding and usability, measure adoption and improve from real-world feedback. 

Keeping AI products reliable and viable. Define good agent performance, understand cost and latency, set up evaluation and monitoring with Engineering, and trade off autonomy, reliability, human intervention and cost. 

Owning strategy, roadmap and delivery in your scope, with clear specs, a definition of done and impact analysis. 

Working with Engineering on trade-offs, dependencies, quality and our API-first AI-first architecture. 

Balancing ambition with reality. Weigh the roadmap against operational requests, bugs and technical debt, and say no to good ideas that aren't great ones. 

Spotting dependencies early with Hotel Operations and other engineering teams, since our AI capabilities build on the core platform. 

Using AI in your own PM work and championing AI-assisted engineering. 

What you'll bring 

6+ years as a Product Manager, owning products from discovery through launch and adoption with limited day-to-day direction. 

Proven zero-to-one experience. You've taken a new B2B product, not a feature, from an ambiguous problem to paying customers, driving discovery, validation, definition, prioritisation and launch. 

Ownership after launch. You've owned a revenue, adoption or retention number and can tell us what moved and what you killed, pivoted or repriced. 

Commercial thinking. You've defined propositions, packaging and pricing, validated willingness to pay and worked with Sales, Marketing and Customer Success on go-to-market. 

Systems and process thinking. You break processes into steps, decisions and handoffs, and understand how systems with different data models and sources of truth affect the reliability of agents. 

Meaningful AI product experience. You've built and launched AI-powered products or capabilities used by real customers, understand what makes a product agentic, and can discuss context, tools, latency, cost and evaluation, with a view on human-in-the-loop design. 

Customer centricity and product judgement. You turn interview patterns into opportunities, make tough trade-offs and prioritise ruthlessly. 

Platform thinking. You weigh customer needs against reusable capabilities, API consistency and long-term platform evolution. 

Stakeholder alignment. You align Engineering, commercial teams and peers, manage cross-team dependencies and communicate trade-offs with confidence. 

Autonomy and adaptability. You take ownership, raise risks early and make progress through ambiguity. 

Strongly preferred 

Agentic AI products in production. You've taken an agentic AI product beyond prototype to paying customers, and dealt with reliability, permissions, exceptions, human intervention and evaluation. This is different from AI-powered features such as chatbots, summarisation or copilots. 

 

Nice to have 

Hospitality technology or hotel operations experience. 

Experience with PMS, RMS, CRS, channel managers, OTAs or hospitality distribution. 

Experience in B2B SaaS platforms, ecosystems or integration-heavy products. 

Experience with AI governance, permissions, identity, orchestration or enterprise AI adoption. 

Experience in a fast-moving startup or scale-up. 

Comfort with AI-assisted engineering processes. 

Don't tick every box? Hospitality experience is an advantage, not a prerequisite. A strong zero-to-one B2B product builder from another domain, with real AI product experience and a commercial mindset, can be a better fit than a hospitality specialist without them. We'd still love to hear from you. 

Who you are 

You take high ownership. You answer for product outcomes, not just delivery commitments. 

You're strategic and hands-on. You can set a product vision and still get into customer discovery, operational processes and detailed product decisions. 

You're comfortable with ambiguity. You make progress when the problem or the solution isn't fully defined. 

You think commercially. You ask what customers will buy and why, not just what Engineering can build. 

You're customer obsessed. You understand real operational pain and test your assumptions with customers. 

You're technically curious. You know enough about AI and agentic systems to hold meaningful discussions with engineers and make informed product decisions. 

You measure what matters. You judge success by customer outcomes, adoption and commercial impact, not features shipped. 

What we offer 

Culture and growth 

A diverse and international team. Work alongside passionate professionals from over 20 nationalities, bringing unique perspectives and experiences to shape the future of hospitality tech. 

Growth and development. You'll benefit from 360° feedback reviews, a dedicated learning budget and plenty of chances to take on more responsibility. 

Autonomy and ownership. Great ideas can come from anywhere. We empower you to take responsibility, make decisions and contribute directly, in an environment built on trust and transparency. 

Competitive and fair compensation. Our salaries are competitive and guided by benchmarking data to ensure fairness across all roles and teams. 

Perks and lifestyle 

Flexible and remote work options. We focus on results, not clocking hours. Work from home, the office or in a hybrid setup. 

Free public transport. Travel across Germany with a fully covered Deutschland Ticket. 

Paid time off. 30 days of vacation to fully disconnect, recharge and return inspired. 

Health and wellbeing. Access to hundreds of gyms, fitness studios and wellness options through our EGYM Wellpass membership. 

Joining Apaleo 

How you make an impact joining Apaleo: Joining Apaleo is more than taking on a role. It's about driving real change in the hospitality industry. Your contributions will directly shape our innovative platform, influence company-wide decisions and help redefine the future of hospitality tech. 

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer, committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive and welcoming workplace. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of race, colour, religion, gender identity or expression, sex, national origin, age, marital status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Your personal data will be handled with the utmost care and in compliance with GDPR and relevant data protection regulations. We celebrate differences and believe that diversity enriches our team and drives innovation.

No mystery ingredients. No shortcuts. Just clean, thoughtfully made formula that parents can trust.

But Bobbie has never been just a formula company. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

We're a company that genuinely believes becoming a parent makes you an activist. The people who work here feel that too.

As the Director of Innovation on Bobbie’s New Ventures team reporting to the President, New Ventures, you will help build the next chapters of Bobbie’s growth by identifying and launching new categories, products, formats, and business models that expand where and how we can serve families. You will own innovation from opportunity identification through market validation, bringing together consumer insight, product development, business strategy, and go-to-market execution to turn promising ideas into viable new businesses.

This role goes beyond getting a product to launch. You will own the go-to-market strategy, performance reporting, and test and learn agenda after launch, using real consumer behavior and business performance to determine what we iterate, scale, or stop.

Your job is to answer: Where should Bobbie play next? What should we build? And have we proven it deserves to scale? Once an innovation has demonstrated strong consumer demand and a viable path to scale, you will lead the transition into Bobbie’s core studio for ongoing brand management and growth.

What you will accomplish: 

Build Bobbie’s New Ventures Innovation Pipeline

Identify high potential consumer needs and translate them into opportunities for Bobbie to enter new categories and formats.

Build and manage a focused innovation pipeline grounded in consumer problems, category dynamics, cultural trends, competitive activity, and Bobbie’s long term strategy.

Develop opportunity spaces and concepts, pressure testing consumer desirability, strategic fit, feasibility, and commercial potential.

Build business cases, financial models, pricing strategies, and success criteria to determine which opportunities Bobbie should pursue.

Lead consumer research, concept development, prototyping, and validation to strengthen opportunities before commercialization.

Bring New Categories & Formats to Market

Serve as the business lead for new innovations from concept through commercialization and early market validation.

Lead cross functional teams across R&D, Clinical, Insights, Marketing, Creative, Growth, Commercial, Operations, Finance, Regulatory, and Customer Experience.

Define the consumer proposition, positioning, pricing, channel strategy, and business model for each new venture.

Own the go-to-market strategy for new innovations, including audience, channel, launch sequencing, trial strategy, investment requirements, and measurement.

Drive cross functional launch readiness and ensure the business is set up to learn quickly once an innovation reaches the market.

Own Test, Learn & In Market Validation

Define the consumer and business hypotheses each innovation needs to prove before launch.

Own post launch performance reporting across trial, acquisition, repeat, retention, revenue, margin, and other venture specific KPIs.

Build and lead the test and learn roadmap, using consumer feedback and real world performance to optimize the product, proposition, pricing, channel, and GTM model.

Translate performance into clear recommendations on what to iterate, scale, or stop.

Capture and apply learnings across the broader New Ventures pipeline so each launch makes Bobbie better at building the next one.

Prove New Businesses & Transition Them to the Core

Establish clear criteria for when an innovation has demonstrated sufficient consumer demand, repeatability, and commercial viability to scale.

Build the case for continued investment as ventures move from incubation into growth.

Lead the transition of proven innovations into the core studio, including the business strategy, consumer learning, performance baseline, growth opportunities, and roadmap.

Partner through the transition while shifting ongoing ownership to the core studio, allowing New Ventures to focus on building Bobbie’s next growth opportunity.

Build Bobbie’s Innovation Engine

Create repeatable ways of working that allow Bobbie to identify, build, launch, and learn from new innovations faster.

Bring consumers into the development process early and often, from identifying unmet needs through concept development and post launch learning.

Build strong external partnerships with suppliers, manufacturers, experts, research partners, and other collaborators that unlock new capabilities.

Bring a portfolio mindset to New Ventures, balancing longer term category expansion with nearer term opportunities that can unlock incremental growth.

What we would like you to have: 

8-10 years of experience in product marketing, innovation, or brand management within CPG, ideally in food or nutrition; experience in infant, toddler or maternal health is a plus.

3+ years leading or managing cross-functional teams and direct reports

Proven track record of bringing new products from concept through commercialization via a Stage Gate or similar innovation process

Experience building and executing product roadmaps that balance innovation with portfolio optimization/renovation

Experience with product positioning frameworks, competitive analysis, and category management tools (e.g., IRI/Circana, Nielsen, SPINS)

Ability to build and present compelling ROI analyses and financial models to leadership

Working knowledge of regulatory considerations in food/infant nutrition (FDA labeling, claims compliance) is a strong plus

Comfortable with data visualization and presentation tools for executive-level storytelling

Familiarity with co-manufacturing relationships and how product innovation intersects with operations and supply chain constraints

You’re inspired by our core values:

Be Radical - We are change makers, rule breakers and stigma shakers. We are unapologetically bold and use our megaphone for good.

Nurture the Tension - Parenthood is full of healthy tension, and so is building a company. We embrace the unknowns, practice humility and are a culture of learners.

Deliver Ounce by Ounce - Our customers have entrusted us to feed their babies. We lose sleep over the details, so they don’t have to.

Don’t Assume - We embrace our unique perspectives, withhold judgment, and find beauty in the paths that brought us all to Bobbie. Our strength is celebrating each other and our collective voice.

Compensation and Benefits:

Compensation 

Our salaries are based on paying competitively for our size and industry. For fully remote roles, we have a single salary target per role that is differentiated based on geographic location (Group A, B, or C).

jobs.description:
About the Job:

Most companies don’t have a “release problem” so much as a way-of-working problem. Shipping live functionality to their customers takes too long, depends on a few heroes, or happens with fingers crossed, and AI-assisted development is raising the stakes. LaunchDarkly Professional Services is helping our most strategic customers change that, and we’re hiring a Release Strategist to lead those engagements.

As a Release Strategist on LaunchDarkly's Professional Services team, you are the “product manager” for each customer engagement, responsible for defining how that customer achieves release excellence by evolving their software and agentic release processes. You join the sales cycle early to define the problem and quantify what it’s costing them, then own the engagement through delivery and adoption until the change sticks. You own the “why” and the “what”; our Solutions Architects, who serve as our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), own the “how.”

Day to day, you’ll partner with a Solutions Architect on each engagement, combining their technical judgment with your view of the commercial context, customer priorities, and relationship dynamics. Neither of you can do the job alone. You own the problem, the value, the scope, and the success criteria; your Solutions Architect owns the technical approach and its quality. You’ll also work closely with Account Executives and Customer Success Managers, and you’ll lead without direct authority, so influence, clarity, and trust matter more than title.

This is a new role, and its shape will flex and adapt as the business grows. Early on, expect to lean into scoping, delivery, and change leadership on both the pre-sales and post-sales side of the business. As we establish a feedback loop through customer delivery, you’ll extend that product mindset from individual engagements to our offerings themselves, and help write the playbook for how we package engagements, measure success, and bring on the next Release Strategist.

Responsibilities:

Product & Value

Scope the problem and the value if solved: join sales cycles from early discovery, map the customer’s organization and decision landscape, and quantify the business value of their release and delivery problem.

Define the customer engagement like a product: identify the business challenges and, with your Solutions Architect, the technical ones behind them; set the MVP or first phase, success criteria, and timeline; write the engagement plan (the outcomes, deliverables, and acceptance criteria the team delivers against); and shape the SOW with PS leadership so what we sell is what we can deliver.

Own scope and prioritization: decide what we do first and what we defer, manage scope as the engagement evolves, and continuously assess whether it still serves both the customer’s outcomes and LaunchDarkly’s interests, reshaping the plan when they diverge.

Own the outcome from go-live, the point where the customer starts working the new way, through adoption: capture feedback, iterate, and prove the business value defined at the start.

Change & Adoption

Facilitate discovery and design sessions mapping release processes and visualizing “who should get a feature and when” without the technology or process on how to accomplish it. Adapt or invent new collaborative practices when a customer’s situation doesn’t fit one we already use, to turn ambiguous goals into clear, owned success plans.

Lead and grow our change management practices: align customer teams on new ways of working, address resistance, and drive adoption so changes stick after the engagement ends. Scope the ongoing support plan and create the documentation and enablement the customer needs to sustain it.

Executive & Growth

Act as a trusted advisor to VP and C-level stakeholders: set expectations, present progress, risks, recommend data-driven decisions, and drive decisions quickly.

Monitor account health and surface expansion or renewal signals; scope the next engagement as a natural outcome of delivered value.

Offerings & Playbook (grows as our FDE engagement volume does)

Turn what you learn across engagements into a feedback loop for our offerings: capture patterns, help shape how we package engagements and measure success, and help write the playbook, including how we bring on future hires.

Delivery & Execution

Run the delivery rhythm: status calls and reporting, accountability to tasks and deadlines across the engagement team, and escalation of technical or political blockers.

Keep a running view of budget/burn against SOW and flag over/under-projection early; partner with PM-type support (where it exists on an account) for detailed tracking and change-order mechanics.

Customer Landscape

Our customers struggle with long lead times, risky deployments, feature flag sprawl, unclear ownership of releases, and a gap between what engineering ships and what the business expects. You’ll need to speak confidently about CI/CD, progressive delivery, testing and quality gates, how agent-generated changes affect release risk, and delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. You don’t need to write the code. You do need to know when a customer is describing a real constraint and when they’re describing a habit.

Qualifications:

Core

8+ years of relevant experience, ideally in senior, client-facing roles across product management, delivery, or consulting within B2B SaaS or technology services; or as a forward-deployed/deployment strategist, or early builder/founder at a high-growth tech startup.

Product and systems thinking: you can define what to deliver and why (MVP or first-phase scoping, prioritization, and success criteria) and manage scope against it.

Value-based scoping experience (ROI/TCO) with executive buyers, ideally within sales cycles.

A track record owning both delivery accountability and the executive relationship on the same engagement, with the judgment to decide whether an engagement’s scope still serves the business, not just execute against an agreed plan. Executive-level communication and presence.

You’ve helped an organization move off an entrenched process and adopt a new way of working, not just documented a better one, including facilitating workshops with mixed engineering and leadership groups and adapting formats on the fly.

Regular, practical use of AI tools in your work, with good judgment about their limits.

Enough confidence in SDLC and software delivery to be credible with technical stakeholders, and experience partnering closely with technical roles (solutions engineers, architects, or similar).

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with progressive delivery and feature management, ideally including LaunchDarkly or a similar tool. Fluency with delivery metrics such as deployment frequency, lead time, and change-failure rate. We’ll teach you the LaunchDarkly specifics.

Demonstrated fluency with AI tooling to analyze data, generate insights, and build visualizations and narratives, with sound judgment about accuracy and appropriate use.

Experience writing PRDs and managing agile software projects.

Experience surfacing expansion/renewal signals to Sales or AM; comfort with a role that may take on commercial ownership over time.

(Bonus) Experience operating in a scaling PS org where role boundaries are still being defined.

Travel

Travel roughly once per quarter for customer workshops and team onsites; more frequent travel may be needed around specific engagements.

Pay:

Target pay ranges based on Geographic Zones* for Level P4:

Zone 1: San Francisco/Bay Area or NYC Metropolitan Area, Boston, Seattle - $171,200- $235,400**

Zone 2: Irvine, LA, Monterey, Santa Barbara, Santa Rosa, Austin, Portland, Philadelphia, Chicago - $154,100 - $211,860**

Zone 3: All other US locations - $145,500 - $200,090**

LaunchDarkly operates from a place of high trust and transparency; we are happy to state the pay range for our open roles to best align with your needs. Exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, and location.

*Within the United States, our geographic pay zones are defined by counties surrounding major metropolitan areas.
**Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), health, vision, and dental insurance, and mental health benefits in addition to salary.

About LaunchDarkly:

Modern software delivery was supposed to be the foundation for a thriving digital business but reality has proven otherwise. Slow, inefficient development cycles, costly outages, and fragmented customer experiences are preventing developers from building their best software. The LaunchDarkly platform helps developers innovate on new features faster while protecting them with a safety valve to instantly rewind when things go wrong. Developers can target product experiences to any customer segment and maximize the business impact of every feature. And by gradually rolling out new application components, they escape nightmare "big-bang" technology migrations. 

The LaunchDarkly platform was built to guide engineers to the next frontier of DevOps by:

Improving the velocity and stability of software releases, without the fear of end customer outages

Delivering targeted experiences by easily personalizing features to customer cohorts

Maximizing the business impact of every feature through the ability to experiment and optimize

Coordinating the release and optimization of software to provide consistent experiences across mobile platforms and device types

Improving the effectiveness and productivity of engineering teams, by providing insights into engineering cadence and stability

At LaunchDarkly, we believe in the power of teams. We're building a team that is humble, open, collaborative, respectful and kind. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. LD invites any applicant to review our written Affirmative Action Plan. To do so, contact People Ops at hr@launchdarkly.com. 

Do you need a disability accommodation?

Fill out this accommodations request form and someone from our People Operations team will contact you for assistance. 

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, LaunchDarkly recruiters will only contact you from @LaunchDarkly.com email addresses or via LinkedIn from "Verified Recruiter" accounts. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate LaunchDarkly recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before making a job offer. LaunchDarkly will never make a job offer without conducting a formal interview process. Our interview process does not involve asking detailed questions by email. If you are ever unsure about a communication that you receive, don't click any links—visit Careers | LaunchDarkly directly for confirmed job openings and links to apply.

Please notify us of any fraudulent representation by sending an email to careers@launchdarkly.com.

Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake. 

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role in a nutshell:

At Chainguard we're focused on securing the software supply chain. Our growing developer community reflects the genuine passion of users sharing their successes, best practices and innovation around the tools they use. We're hiring a Developer Outreach Lead for a high-impact, highly technical role that puts the needs of developers and their communities at the heart of everything we do: building new and lasting relationships with developers, community leaders and the organizations where our users get the most benefit and support.

This is a player-coach role. You'll lead our outreach programs from day one with potential to build a team around you as the function grows. Reporting to the Head of DevRel, you'll join a highly collaborative, world-class Developer Relations team. As someone developers know and trust, you'll bring technical credibility to help builders get hands-on. You'll be a vital link between Chainguard and the developer communities we serve, working hand in hand with our product, engineering and marketing teams.

What you'll do

Build our strategy to engage and support the communities that matter most to our users

Start with what developers need, and build outreach programs that lead help developers go from a first look to secure workflows.

Establish genuine relationships with community leaders, meetup organizers, open-source maintainers and foundation members, and nurture them over the long term so Chainguard is a trusted partner, not just a sponsor

Represent Chainguard at meetups, conferences and partner events across the Bay Area and beyond, with roughly 40% travel

Manage programs that recognize our most passionate and knowledgeable community members, and extend our reach into developer and DevOps communities

Show up where practitioners already are (GitHub, Reddit, LinkedIn, community forums, conferences and meetups) and be a trusted voice there by publishing tutorials, giving talks and showing code

Track activation and sustained usage from your programs, and double down on what helps developers succeed

Be the voice of the developer inside Chainguard, bringing community feedback to product and engineering so what we build reflects what developers actually need

Partner across our Marketing org (product marketing, brand and social) and GTM teams to align community efforts with our go-to-market motion and help us scale programs with target accounts

What we're looking for

A proven record of driving developer adoption: programs, engagement or content that led people to actually use something, beyond views and likes

A public body of work: code shared on GitHub, plus technical videos, tutorials or talks you've delivered

7+ years of technical experience with a true software engineering foundation

5+ years building technical communities and ambassador or champion programs, whether in DevRel, technical instruction or professional services

An established personal brand with deep influence in at least one developer channel like GitHub, LinkedIn, Reddit or community forums (a leadership or advisory board role in a framework community like Python or Django counts too)

Active involvement in DevOps or application security communities, with trusted, long-term relationships with meetup organizers, community leaders and open-source maintainers. You're already in the circle

Outgoing, personable and highly collaborative: you thrive working across product, engineering and marketing, and you lead with empathy for what developers need

Hands-on experience with AI agents and a point of view on how developers are enabling them today

Nice to have

DevRel leadership experience, as both a program lead and people manager

Maintainer or leading contributor to an open-source project, ideally in the DevOps or application security space

Experience with our ecosystem partners

Familiarity supporting account-based programs alongside a go-to-market team

Base Salary Range

$151,000—$178,000 USD

About Us

We live and breathe our company values:

We are customer obsessed — We focus on delivering solutions to our customers that create value and make their lives better.

We have a bias for intentional action — We prioritize, plan, try things, and fail fast.

We don't take ourselves too seriously (but we do serious work) — We are solving an important problem which takes focus, but we also like to enjoy the journey.

We trust each other and assume good intentions — We're transparent with decisions to empower team members to make well informed decisions.

A few of the benefits we offer:

Flexible & Remote-First Culture: Work remotely with team meetup opportunities, bi-annual destination summits, and a monthly stipend for coworking spaces, phone and internet costs.

Our Approach to Equity: Receive stock options upon hire and promotion. Plus, you can participate in secondary offerings and have 10 years to exercise your options (yes, you read that correctly: 10 years!).

100% Covered Health Insurance: We cover 100% of your health, vision and dental insurance premiums for you and your dependents. Nothing comes out of your paycheck.

∞ Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need – to do our best work, we need to recharge and reset.

18 Weeks Paid Parental Leave: We offer 18 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents, with the option to use it all at once or throughout your child's first year.

If your experience is close but doesn't fulfill all requirements, please apply. We're building the best team in technology and are focused on hiring "Chainguardians" with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.

We're looking for an Onboarding Manager - German speaking (f/m/d) to join our team in Munich! This job is a great opportunity for professionals willing to take the next step in their careers. You will report to our Team Lead Onboarding.

What You’ll Be Up To:

jobs.description:
About Bobbie

Bobbie makes European-style organic infant formula manufactured end-to-end in the U.S., because we believe every parent deserves to feed their baby with confidence, without judgment and without compromise. No mystery ingredients. No shortcuts. Just clean, thoughtfully made formula that parents can trust.

But Bobbie has never been just a formula company. When the 2022 national infant formula shortage left parents across the country unable to feed their babies, we closed our storefront to new customers rather than leave a single existing family without formula. We went to Washington. We got loud. And we opened our Heath, Ohio manufacturing facility to make sure something like that could never happen again.

That's who we are, and that's what you'd be joining.

Bobbie for Change

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. We fight for paid federal parental leave, push for legislation to prevent future formula shortages, advocate for feeding equity, and support families navigating impossible situations, including donating formula to parents impacted by breast and gynecologic cancers through the Bobbie Breasties program.

We're a company that genuinely believes becoming a parent makes you an activist. The people who work here feel that too.

The Role

We’re looking for the person who wakes up every day thinking about how to make the Bobbie experience better, and who partners closely with Product, Lifecycle, Creative and Development to make it happen.

You’re obsessed with our customers and driven by insight. You’ll be the voice of parents in every design decision. You’ll spend as much time understanding them (what confuses them, what worries them, what makes them stay or leave) as you spend in Figma, and you’ll turn that understanding into clear problem statements, sharp prioritization and well-crafted experiences.

You’re proactive. You don’t wait for a brief. You spot friction in the data, in support tickets or in a usability session, and you bring the problem, plus a point of view on how to solve it, to the table before anyone asks.

You’ll lead and rebuild our in-house UX/UI function, setting the standards, workflows and design culture the rest of the team builds on. You’ll own our design system and Figma hygiene end to end, starting with a new foundation, and bring personalization into the subscriber journey.

What You’ll Do

Lead the in-house UX/UI function

Act as Bobbie’s in-house UX/UI lead. Set the design vision, quality bar and ways of working as we rebuild the function.

Establish and evangelize UX/UI best practices, accessibility standards (WCAG) and design workflows across the product organization, staying current with industry trends and emerging tools.

Direct our ongoing UX/UI agency partner: set priorities, give clear creative and quality feedback, and raise the bar on their work.

Mentor designers and contractors, and be the go-to design partner for leadership.

Design across the subscriber journey

Design wireframes, prototypes and user flows to communicate ideas. Identify and fix UX/UI issues across the conversion funnel: homepage, product, cart and checkout pages.

Partner with Product Managers and Lifecycle Marketing to shape the subscriber journey, designing key moments across it: signup, plan management, billing, feeding-stage transitions, save flows, cancellation and winback.

Bring design and customer insight to personalization, working with Product and Lifecycle on experiences that adapt to each family’s stage and needs, onsite and throughout the subscription.

Build and own the design system

Own Bobbie’s design system end to end. Start by auditing it and rebuilding its foundation so the team can move faster without losing quality.

Develop and maintain design systems, style guides and UI patterns for consistency across mobile and web, with a mobile-first approach to visual design.

Own Figma file hygiene and design system integrity (components, tokens, documentation and naming conventions) so the system stays scalable and easy for any collaborator to pick up.

Research and validation

Plan and run qualitative and quantitative research (usability testing, subscriber interviews, funnel and behavioral analysis) to validate design decisions and improve conversion, retention and satisfaction across the subscription funnel.

Turn what you learn into clear problem statements and bring them to Product as opportunities, not just design requests.

Run competitor analysis, gather user feedback and use A/B testing to keep improving design and usability. Always look for new ways to remove friction from our UX.

Keep Bobbie’s parent community at the core of the UX, designing the subscription journey around their needs, feedback and voice.

Platform: Work with designers, Product Managers and Engineers early and often to validate technical feasibility, scope tradeoffs and make sure designs ship with fidelity across mobile and web.

Lifecycle: Design cohesive experiences across owned channels (email, SMS, web) that reduce churn, increase reactivation and support parents through every stage of their subscription.

Brand and Product Marketing: Partner with Brand on brand and commercial strategy, and with Product Marketing so the subscription experience supports go-to-market priorities and stays true to Bobbie’s positioning.

Project and process leadership

Clearly explain and justify design decisions, breaking features down into MVPs that deliver immediate value.

Set clear timelines for UX/UI deliverables, managing dependencies and blockers while leading projects through the design phase.

What You Bring

Customer obsession you can show. A portfolio where you can point to the customer insight behind each decision and what you learned after launch, not just the final screens.

Proactive problem-solving. Examples of problems you spotted and pushed forward yourself, and the outcome they drove.

Strategic rigor. You frame problems clearly, weigh tradeoffs against business goals like conversion and retention, and hold your own in roadmap conversations with Product and leadership.

Experience leading a design function. You’ve built or led an in-house UX/UI practice: setting standards and workflows, directing agencies or contractors, and mentoring designers.

Senior craft. Deep UX and UI skills across web and mobile, expert Figma skills, and experience building scalable design systems.

Personalized, data-driven design. Experience designing personalized or data-driven experiences, and using data to shape decisions and measure results.

Relevant experience. Significant product design experience, ideally in DTC subscription, membership or other recurring-revenue products. Mobile-first design experience is strongly preferred.

Clear communication. You can tell the story behind a design decision to any audience.

While Also Being

Passionate — about what we are doing.

Proactive — can take initiative to get things done.

Curious — love learning and staying on top of emerging trends.

Excited about working at an early-stage startup — where you may end up doing all kinds of things!

Health, baby/parenting, or CPG/ecommerce experience

Why This Role Matters

At Bobbie, design isn't decoration — it's the thing standing between a parent and their baby's next meal. Every flow you design determines whether a subscriber gets their formula on time, understands their options during a stressful moment, or feels supported through a feeding-stage change. This role sits at the center of Creative, Platform, and Lifecycle because the subscription experience only works when all three tell one consistent story.

You’re inspired by our core values:

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

We are seeking an experienced Commercial Counsel to join our Legal Team in Brazil. In this role, you will support complex commercial transactions with a primary focus on Brazil and support for other LATAM countries, including SaaS, licensing, and strategic partnerships, while helping the company navigate diverse legal and regulatory frameworks in the rapidly evolving field of artificial intelligence. Who you are

Curious about the future of AI and emerging technologies, have a strong sense of ownership with enthusiasm for applying your legal expertise to cutting-edge products.

Experienced in navigating fast-paced, high-growth environments, with the ability to manage ambiguity and make informed, timely decisions.

Comfortable working independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional and global colleagues.

Proactive, business-minded, and committed to delivering practical solutions that support both compliance and commercial success.

Hunger to be exceptional at your job.

What you bring

Law degree and qualification to practice law in Brazil.

Native-level Portuguese and fluent English; Spanish is strongly preferred.

7+ years of relevant post-qualification legal experience (in-house experience in technology or SaaS strongly preferred).

Proven track record drafting and negotiating complex commercial and technology agreements.

Strong knowledge of enterprise software licensing, SaaS, data protection, and intellectual property.

Experience advising on privacy, cybersecurity, and cross-border data transfer issues.

Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.

jobs.description:
Not all heroes wear capes — but plenty of them use toilet paper

Want to challenge yourself at a purpose-led scale up AND make a difference in the world? Come join the revolootion!

Funny name, serious business

We are a leading eco-friendly household essentials business and we donate 50% of our profits to help everyone gain access to clean water and a toilet. As of June 2024, we’ve contributed over $20 million AUD to this mission. Basically, we’re really good at making it easy to do good.

We operate scaling businesses the UK, US, Australia and Canada. Our amazing team is based in Australia, the UK, the Philippines, China, and the US. Our 250+ people aim to make the biggest possible impact for people and the planet. Over the next 5-10 years, we’re hoping to increase our annual donation tenfold to get us closer to our dream of everyone in the world having access to clean water and sanitation services.

A bit about the role

As our AR & AP Lead, you’ll be the eyes and ears of our Number Scrunchers accounting function — driving accounts receivable and accounts payable operations day to day, in close partnership with your two direct reports (our AR Expert and AP Coordinator) and the wider Financial Operations team. You’ll keep our books accurate, our customers paying on time, and our suppliers paid on time, all so we can maximise the donations we’re able to make.

If you worked here this past month here are some things you might have been involved in

Pulled together the monthly AR ageing report for the CFO and exec team, with a clear plan to chase down aged amounts

Reviewed the weekly payments file (including the Tipalti funding summary) before it went out for approval

Flagged an “at risk” customer account early and looped in the customer-facing team for support

Helped close the books accurately and on time at month-end, escalating one risk early to the Head of Financial Operations

Worked with the AP Coordinator to tidy up a clunky step in the AP process

Let’s talk about you

Detail is your love language 

You get real satisfaction from a reconciliation that ties out perfectly and a report that lands on the CFO’s desk without a single follow-up question. You’re equally comfortable rolling your sleeves up in the detail of a customer account and stepping back to build the KPIs and reporting that keep the whole team honest.

Calm under a closing calendar 

Month-end doesn’t rattle you. You know how to keep AR and AP on track to a deadline, spot a risk early enough to actually do something about it, and communicate clearly with stakeholders when something needs to change.

A coach as much as a doer 

You lead a small, tight-knit team and genuinely enjoy it — you give clear, kind feedback, help your people grow, and aren’t afraid of a difficult conversation when a process or a stakeholder relationship needs a repair job.

You give a crap.

Do you want your work to make the world a better place? Do you want to work with other people who feel the same way? What a coincidence — us too!

Why should you work with us?

First off, as a certified B Corp™, we work to make a difference every day while maintaining the high standards of social and environmental impact. We’re in very good company with other exceptional B Corps around the world.

We also believe that helping to make the world a better place should be rewarded accordingly – that’s why we offer competitive, market informed salaries, meaningful support towards healthcare for our team around the world, generous paid leave, tailored learning and development opportunities, and free toilet paper (yes, you read that right).

Our engagement surveys (thanks Culture Amp!) tell us that our team is really proud (over 90%) to work for Who Gives A Crap and, well, we couldn’t be more proud of that.

Have you made it this far?

If you’re still reading, we think there’s a strong chance you might be our kind of person. Here’s the thing, though — research suggests that 60% of women and underrepresented folks might have already talked themselves out of applying. Even if you don’t check every box above, we want to encourage you to introduce yourself. We believe a diversity of perspectives and experiences makes a team stronger — and the stronger our team, the closer we are to delivering toilets and clean water for all.

Consistent creation of qualified enterprise pipeline across Germany

Strong control of complex sales cycles from first conversation through close

A clear market-ownership mindset, with the initiative to build relationships, awareness, and opportunity in territory

Executive presence in both German and English, with the ability to sell business value, resilience, risk reduction, and investment justification

Track record of winning complex enterprise deals, exceeding growth targets, and delivering consistent quota attainment over multiple years

Experience engaging C-suite, senior leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders across security, identity, infrastructure, and risk

Strong prospecting, market development, and territory-planning capability

Ability to build and execute account-based and territory-based strategies

Technical and commercial credibility with both technical and business stakeholders

High degree of ownership and self-leadership, with the ability to operate effectively in a high-growth or scale-up environment

Clear, credible, and outcome-oriented communication style with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders

jobs.description:
About Truelogic

At Truelogic we are a leading provider of nearshore staff augmentation services headquartered in New York. For over two decades, we’ve been delivering top-tier technology solutions to companies of all sizes, from innovative startups to industry leaders, helping them achieve their digital transformation goals.

Our team of 600+ highly skilled tech professionals, based in Latin America, drives digital disruption by partnering with U.S. companies on their most impactful projects. Whether collaborating with Fortune 500 giants or scaling startups, we deliver results that make a difference.

By applying for this position, you’re taking the first step in joining a dynamic team that values your expertise and aspirations. We aim to align your skills with opportunities that foster exceptional career growth and success while contributing to transformative projects that shape the future.

Our Client

Our client is a leading provider of intelligent software solutions, helping organizations transform how they manage training, compliance, and operational excellence. We are committed to data integrity, performance, and innovation in every product we deliver. As part of our growing data quality team, you’ll help ensure that the data driving our platforms is accurate, secure, and reliable.

Job Summary

We are looking for a Data QA Engineer to safeguard the integrity, accuracy, and reliability of our data ecosystems. In this role, you will tackle the key challenge of validating complex ETL pipelines, ensuring seamless data migrations, and verifying that transformed data reflects true business logic before reaching analytical layers and decision-makers.

Responsibilities

Data Validation & Verification: Ensure data accuracy, consistency, and completeness across pipelines. Validate ETL processes, referential integrity, constraints, and data normalization.

Database Testing: Perform functional testing on stored procedures, triggers, views, and functions. Test data migrations, data warehousing systems, and write complex SQL queries to verify data correctness.

ETL & BI Testing: Validate data pipelines, transformations, and business logic within reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) to ensure accurate report generation.

Automation of Database Tests: Build and maintain automated test scripts for database regression and integration testing.

Performance Monitoring: Identify slow-running queries, monitor execution plans, evaluate indexing, and collaborate with DBAs to fine-tune system performance.

Collaboration & Quality Standards: Partner with developers, DBAs, data analysts, and product teams to document defects in JIRA/TestRail and drive data quality best practices.

Qualifications and Job Requirements

Strong SQL Expertise: Advanced ability to write and execute complex SQL queries for deep data verification and reconciliation.

Playwright / Python / Typescript / AI-forward testers

ETL & Data Warehouse Testing: Proven experience validating ETL/ELT data pipelines, transformation logic, and data warehousing environments.

Database Functional Testing: Hands-on experience testing core database objects such as stored procedures, views, triggers, and functions.

Data Integrity & Structure: Solid understanding of data normalization, referential integrity, and data schema validation.

QA Lifecycle & Tooling: Practical experience documenting test cases, results, and defects in management tools like JIRA or TestRail.

What We Offer

100% Remote Work: Enjoy the freedom to work from the location that helps you thrive. All it takes is a laptop and a reliable internet connection.

Highly Competitive USD Pay: Earn an excellent, market-leading compensation in USD, that goes beyond typical market offerings.

Paid Time Off: We value your well-being. Our paid time off policies ensure you have the chance to unwind and recharge when needed.

Work with Autonomy: Enjoy the freedom to manage your time as long as the work gets done. Focus on results, not the clock.

Work with Top American Companies: Grow your expertise working on innovative, high-impact projects with Industry-Leading U.S. Companies.

Why You’ll Like Working Here

A Culture That Values You: We prioritize well-being and work-life balance, offering engagement activities and fostering dynamic teams to ensure you thrive both personally and professionally.

Diverse, Global Network: Connect with over 600 professionals in 25+ countries, expand your network, and collaborate with a multicultural team from Latin America.

Team Up with Skilled Professionals: Join forces with senior talent. All of our team members are seasoned experts, ensuring you're working with the best in your field.

Apply now!

We are launching a new Home & Auto insurance business unit, and you will build the revenue engine that supports it from the ground up. As Revenue Operations Manager, you will own the 0-to-1 design and implementation of the CRM, sales processes, reporting, and operating workflows that help this business acquire and serve customers at scale.

You will shape how leads enter the funnel, how opportunities move through the sales process, how teams manage customer handoffs, and how leaders understand performance. You will administer and evolve HubSpot, connect it with the tools our teams rely on, and establish the data foundation for a new line of business.

You will work closely with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, and Operations to translate an emerging business model into practical systems and repeatable processes. From defining the first pipeline stages and routing rules to launching dashboards and improving workflows, you will help create the operating backbone for Home & Auto while building scalable standards for the broader revenue organization.

You will be both a systems owner and a business partner: identifying what the business needs next, designing pragmatic solutions, and making sure each process is adopted, measured, and improved over time.

jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly 

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.

Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.

Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.

Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.

Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.

Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.

Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.

Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.
